title: Just one cup
setting: A weekday morning at the office. Mai finds her coworker Yuki looking wrecked and assumes she was out drinking. The real culprit was a late-night coffee, and Yuki has drinks with Kenta tonight.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ohayou, yuki. e, daijoubu? sugoku tsukareteru ne.
lines.ja: おはよう、ユキ。え、大丈夫？すごく疲れてるね。
lines.kana: おはよう、ゆき。え、だいじょうぶ？すごくつかれてるね。
lines.english: Morning, Yuki. Oh, are you okay? You look really tired.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ohayou. un, kinou sanjikan shika nerenakatta n da.
lines.ja: おはよう。うん、昨日三時間しか寝れなかったんだ。
lines.kana: おはよう。うん、きのうさんじかんしかねれなかったんだ。
lines.english: Morning. Yeah, I only got three hours' sleep last night.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, wakatta. osake nonda n desho.
lines.ja: あ、わかった。お酒飲んだんでしょ。
lines.kana: あ、わかった。おさけのんだんでしょ。
lines.english: Oh, I know. You were out drinking, weren't you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uun, osake wa nondenai yo. shigoto ga owaranakute, yoru juuji ni koohii nonjatta no.
lines.ja: ううん、お酒は飲んでないよ。仕事が終わらなくて、夜十時にコーヒー飲んじゃったの。
lines.kana: ううん、おさけはのんでないよ。しごとがおわらなくて、よるじゅうじにコーヒーのんじゃったの。
lines.english: No, I wasn't drinking. My work wasn't finished, so I went and had a coffee at ten at night.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: juuji ni? sore wa nerenai yo. watashi mo, yoru koohii nomu to nerenai n da.
lines.ja: 十時に？それは寝れないよ。私も、夜コーヒー飲むと寝れないんだ。
lines.kana: じゅうじに？それはねれないよ。わたしも、よるコーヒーのむとねれないんだ。
lines.english: At ten? That would keep anyone awake. I can't sleep either if I have coffee at night.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: de ne, ima mo koohii nomitai no. kesa mo nihai nonda kedo.
lines.ja: でね、今もコーヒー飲みたいの。今朝も二杯飲んだけど。
lines.kana: でね、いまもコーヒーのみたいの。けさもにはいのんだけど。
lines.english: And the thing is, I want a coffee right now, too. Even though I had two this morning.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: dame dame! konban mo nerenai yo. kore ageru. mizu nonde.
lines.ja: だめだめ！今晩も寝れないよ。これあげる。水飲んで。
lines.kana: だめだめ！こんばんもねれないよ。これあげる。みずのんで。
lines.english: No, no! You won't sleep tonight either. Here, have this. Drink some water.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou. demo, koohii ga ii naa.
lines.ja: ありがとう。でも、コーヒーがいいなあ。
lines.kana: ありがとう。でも、コーヒーがいいなあ。
lines.english: Thanks. But I'd rather have coffee.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, ocha nomu? asoko ni mugicha aru yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、お茶飲む？あそこに麦茶あるよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、おちゃのむ？あそこにむぎちゃあるよ。
lines.english: Then how about some tea? There's barley tea over there.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, ocha nomu. a, sou ieba konban, kenta-tachi to osake nomu n da.
lines.ja: うん、お茶飲む。あ、そういえば今晩、ケンタたちとお酒飲むんだ。
lines.kana: うん、おちゃのむ。あ、そういえばこんばん、けんたたちとおさけのむんだ。
lines.english: Okay, I'll have tea. Oh, that reminds me, I'm going drinking with Kenta and the others tonight.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, sanjikan shika netenai noni, osake nomu no? dame da yo.
lines.ja: え、三時間しか寝てないのに、お酒飲むの？だめだよ。
lines.kana: え、さんじかんしかねてないのに、おさけのむの？だめだよ。
lines.english: What? You've had three hours' sleep and you're going drinking? No way.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: daijoubu. biiru ippai dake. mizu mo nomu kara.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。ビール一杯だけ。水も飲むから。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。ビールいっぱいだけ。みずものむから。
lines.english: It's fine. Just one beer. And I'll drink water too.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto ni? yuki no ippai dake tte, itsumo sanbai ni naru yo ne.
lines.ja: ほんとに？ユキの「一杯だけ」って、いつも三杯になるよね。
lines.kana: ほんとに？ゆきの「いっぱいだけ」って、いつもさんばいになるよね。
lines.english: Really? Your "just one" always turns into three.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: wakatta yo. konban, osake wa nomanai. ocha dake nomu.
lines.ja: わかったよ。今晩、お酒は飲まない。お茶だけ飲む。
lines.kana: わかったよ。こんばん、おさけはのまない。おちゃだけのむ。
lines.english: Okay, okay. No alcohol tonight. I'll just have tea.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, sore ga ii yo. ato, uchi ni kaettara, mizu nonde sugu nete ne.
lines.ja: うん、それがいいよ。あと、うちに帰ったら、水飲んですぐ寝てね。
lines.kana: うん、それがいいよ。あと、うちにかえったら、みずのんですぐねてね。
lines.english: Yeah, good idea. And when you get home, drink some water and go straight to bed.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un. de, koohii, ippai dake nonde ii?
lines.ja: うん。で、コーヒー、一杯だけ飲んでいい？
lines.kana: うん。で、コーヒー、いっぱいだけのんでいい？
lines.english: Okay. So, can I have just one coffee?

choices.english: Yuki was out drinking last night, so Mai gives her water and tells her to skip tonight's plans.
Yuki couldn't sleep after a late-night coffee, and she agrees to stick to tea at tonight's drinks with Kenta.
Yuki couldn't sleep after a late-night coffee, so she cancels tonight's drinks with Kenta and goes home early.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Mai guesses Yuki was out drinking (osake nonda n desho), but in line 4 Yuki says she wasn't: her work wasn't finished, so she had a coffee at ten at night. In line 10 she remembers she's drinking with Kenta and the others tonight, and after Mai's teasing about her 'just one' (line 13) she decides in line 14: konban, osake wa nomanai. ocha dake nomu. A is Mai's wrong guess from line 3. C goes too far: Yuki still goes out tonight, she just won't drink alcohol; going home and straight to bed is Mai's advice for afterwards (line 15).

questions.english: The morning after a night out, Kenta groans: "Ugh, I drank too much last night. My head hurts." Tell him to drink some water.
questions.ja: ああ、昨日飲みすぎた。頭痛い。
questions.kana: ああ、きのうのみすぎた。あたまいたい。
questions.answer: Tell him to drink water with mizu (o) nomu: check with mizu nonda?, or tell him mizu nonde ne.

modelAnswers.english: Are you okay? Have you had some water?

modelAnswers.romaji: mizu nonde ne. kyou wa osake nomanaide ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 水飲んでね。今日はお酒飲まないでね。
modelAnswers.english: Make sure you drink some water. And no drinking today, okay?

questions.explanation: Drinking water takes the same nomu as every other drink: Mai says mizu nonde (line 7) and uchi ni kaettara, mizu nonde sugu nete ne (line 15), and Yuki promises mizu mo nomu kara (line 12). After a night of drinking, mizu nonda? and mizu nonde ne are what friends say to look after you. Kenta's nomisugita uses nomu on its own: once drinking is the topic, nomu by itself means alcohol. For 'have' a drink, don't reach for motsu or aru; it's always nomu.

questions.english: It's eleven at night at Kenta's flat, and he says: "I'm making coffee. Want some?" Turn it down: tell him you can't sleep if you drink coffee at night.
questions.ja: コーヒー入れるけど、飲む？
questions.kana: コーヒーいれるけど、のむ？
questions.answer: Turn it down with koohii (o) nomu and -to (whenever): yoru koohii nomu to nerenai n da, the line Mai uses.

modelAnswers.romaji: arigatou. demo, yoru koohii nomu to nerenai n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ありがとう。でも、夜コーヒー飲むと寝れないんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Thanks. But I can't sleep if I drink coffee at night.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, ii ya. ima koohii nondara, nerenai kara.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、いいや。今コーヒー飲んだら、寝れないから。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm good. If I have coffee now, I won't be able to sleep.

questions.explanation: Mai says exactly this in line 5: watashi mo, yoru koohii nomu to nerenai n da. Yuki uses the same verb for her late cup in line 4 (yoru juuji ni koohii nonjatta) and asks koohii, ippai dake nonde ii? in line 16. Kenta's ireru is the making (koohii o ireru, ocha o ireru); what you'd be doing is drinking it, so your answer takes nomu.

questions.english: What did Yuki want to drink tonight with Kenta and the others?
questions.ja: ユキさんは今晩、何を飲みたかったですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはこんばん、なにをのみたかったですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa konban, nani o nomitakatta desu ka?
questions.explanation: Line 10: konban, kenta-tachi to osake nomu n da. When Mai objects, Yuki says biiru ippai dake (just one beer, line 12). osake means alcohol in general (beer, wine, highballs); Japanese rice wine specifically is nihonshu. So B is the trap of hearing osake as 'sake'. A is what she agrees to in line 14 (ocha dake nomu) after Mai teases her, not what she wanted.

questions.english: When Yuki says she'd rather have coffee than water, what does Mai offer her instead?
questions.ja: マイさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Then want to go out for a cuppa?

questions.explanation: Line 9: jaa, ocha nomu? asoko ni mugicha aru yo. Yuki takes it in line 10 (un, ocha nomu). ocha is Japanese tea: green tea or, as here, barley tea (mugicha). B, koucha, is black tea, which is what English 'tea' usually means, but ocha never covers it, and it isn't what's on offer. C, ocha shinai?, is an invitation to go out to a cafe for a break; Mai isn't suggesting going anywhere, she's offering the tea that's right there in the office.

newWords.english: barley tea (a Japanese tea, often served cold; no caffeine)
counter for cups and glasses (ippai one, nihai two, sanbai three)
